# Package

`c.Package` calls the API's Package group. The packages installed on the host.

### List

```go
func (s *PackageService) List(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[PackageInstalled]], error)
```

List the packages installed on the host.

Lists each installed package with its version: dpkg on the Debian family, rpm on
the other Linux families, and Homebrew on macOS.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/package`, and needs the permission
`package:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A Debian host, `go run package.go list`:

```go
resp, err := c.Package.List(ctx, target)
```

### Create

```go
func (s *PackageService) Create(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input PackageCreateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[PackageResult]], error)
```

Install a package.

Installs the package with apt-get install, at the version when one is given. A
package that is installed, at that version when one is given, does not change
and reports changed: false. It runs on the Debian family only, and elsewhere
reports skipped.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/package`, and needs the permission
`package:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Install a package, `go run package.go create`:

```go
resp, err := c.Package.Create(ctx, target, client.PackageCreateInput{Name: "tree"})
```

### Get

```go
func (s *PackageService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[PackageInstalled]], error)
```

Get one installed package.

Reads one package from the same list. A package that is not installed is not
found.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/package/{name}`, and needs the permission
`package:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

An installed package, `go run package.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.Package.Get(ctx, target, "curl")
```

An installed formula, `go run package.go get-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Package.Get(ctx, target, "jq")
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *PackageService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[PackageResult]], error)
```

Remove a package.

Removes the package with apt-get remove. A package that is not installed does
not change and reports changed: false. It runs on the Debian family only, and
elsewhere reports skipped.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/package/{name}`, and needs the permission
`package:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Remove a package, `go run package.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.Package.Delete(ctx, target, "tree")
```
